metadata.title: Teacher clusters of emotions and self-efficacy in curriculum reform: Effects on collaboration and learner-centered teaching

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a stratified cluster sampling approach to recruit upper secondary school teachers across different regions and school sizes in Taiwan, followed by voluntary online questionnaire completion in June 2023. The manuscript reports the achieved response count (624 responses out of 640 invited teachers) and provides demographic distributions, but it does not report the use of any TALIS-style sampling weights or complex-survey replicate weights. Because the analyses are based on clustering (Ward + K-means) and subsequent ANOVA/regression, the paper does not describe applying any weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or adjusting standard errors for the complex design. Therefore, readers should treat the results as associations from the obtained sample rather than population-representative estimates unless weighting is confirmed elsewhere.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with ILSA Plausible Values; instead, it models teacher-reported emotions, self-efficacy, collaboration, and learner-centered teaching using Likert-type scales and factor-validated composite scores. As a result, PV handling is not applicable to the dependent variables. The manuscript also does not report a missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation), which is a reporting gap because missingness rules can affect scale composites and cluster membership.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were upper secondary school teachers in Taiwan recruited via stratified cluster sampling across geographical regions and school sizes. After school selection, teachers were invited to complete an online questionnaire in June 2023; the study reports 624 responses out of 640 invited teachers. The manuscript does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., incomplete questionnaires, missing scale items) or any imputation/listwise-deletion rule for missing responses, so the analytic sample is best interpreted as the set of returned responses used for scale scoring and subsequent clustering/regression.

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2018-based teacher scales (Taiwan upper secondary teachers, June 2023 survey)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Cluster-specific regression (Table 6): Cluster 1 R2=0.312; Joy β=0.311 (p<0.001), Self-efficacy β=0.157 (p<0.05). Cluster 2 R2=0.254; Joy β=0.168 (p<0.01), Self-efficacy β=0.193 (p<0.01), Fatigue β=0.140 (p<0.05). Cluster 3 R2=0.222; Joy and Fatigue not significant; Self-efficacy not significant for collaboration. Additional analysis (Learner-centered teaching (composite score)): Cluster-specific regression (Table 6): Cluster 1 R2=0.514; Self-efficacy β=0.671 (p<0.001); Joy not significant; Fatigue not significant. Cluster 2 R2=0.473; Self-efficacy β=0.547 (p<0.001); Joy not significant; Fatigue not significant. Cluster 3 R2=0.480; Self-efficacy β=0.554 (p<0.001); Fatigue β=-0.241 (p<0.05); Joy not significant. Cluster differences via ANOVA (Table 5): Learner-centered teaching F=119.14 (p<0.001), with Cluster 1 > Cluster 2 > Cluster 3.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018-based teacher scales from a Taiwan upper-secondary teacher survey, the study leveraged Joy (teacher emotion), Teacher self-efficacy, and Fatigue (teacher emotion) to predict Teacher collaboration (composite score), finding that joy and self-efficacy were significant positive predictors in Cluster 1 and Cluster 2, while fatigue only mattered in Cluster 2 and no emotion/self-efficacy effects were significant in Cluster 3. This indicates that strengthening teachers’ positive emotional disposition and instructional confidence may support collaborative course design, but effects are heterogeneous across teacher profiles and may require targeted support for low-enthusiasm/low-efficacy teachers.

data.outcome_summary: This study used a stratified cluster sampling survey of 624 upper secondary teachers in Taiwan (June 2023) and employed TALIS 2018-based scales (with modifications) alongside newly developed emotion and learner-centered teaching measures. Teachers were clustered into three profiles using Ward hierarchical clustering followed by K-means on standardized joy, fatigue, and self-efficacy, and then cluster differences were tested with ANOVA and associations were quantified with cluster-specific regressions. For teacher collaboration, joy and self-efficacy predicted higher collaboration in Cluster 1 and Cluster 2 (e.g., Cluster 1 R2=0.312; Cluster 2 R2=0.254), while fatigue only showed a significant effect in Cluster 2 and no predictors were significant in Cluster 3. For learner-centered teaching, self-efficacy was significant across all clusters (Cluster R2≈0.47–0.51), and fatigue negatively predicted learner-centered teaching only in Cluster 3 (β=-0.241, p<0.05). The paper does not report missing-data handling or any survey-weight application, and the design is correlational rather than causal.
